messages:
maria (PM): Heads-up — I'm drafting an initiative to handle short-duration spikes for Dedicated customers without forcing permanent reserves. Working name: 'elastic-buffer' for reserved pools. Goal is: predictable base capacity + small elastic buffer per-pool that can be used for bursts and charged separately.

ajay (backend eng): Quick Q: is buffer per-tenant or per-pool? that affects allocator complexity.

maria (PM): per-pool but with tenant-tagged accounting. customers can opt into buffer billing or buy fixed burst credits.

kevin (sales): customer X asked for something like this — they want a guaranteed base with ability to burst 2x for short windows. they'd pay more for guaranteed burst credits.

ella (customer success): We need clear UX in console for how burst credits are consumed and how customers can top up. Also rollback story if they hit limits.

ajay (backend eng): Implementation notes: allocator needs to track two quotas: reservation and buffer_remaining. Eviction order: best-effort requests -> buffer -> preemptible reserved jobs. If buffer hits zero, fall back to regional hosted or queue.

sasha (SRE): Important: define preemption and SLA. If we allow buffer to be used, we must guarantee base pool latency SLAs remain intact. If buffer consumption threatens SLOs, automatic drain & throttling must trigger.

maria (PM): Agreed. Proposing launch criteria:
- telemetry for buffer usage (per-pool, per-tenant)
- billing events emitted for buffer consumption
- guardrail: buffer can't reduce base capacity below 95% of target SLA window
- canary rollout to 3 internal tenants + 1 pilot customer

ajay (backend eng): Prototype config I sketched: 
```yaml
pool: gpu-a100-40
reservation: 80
buffer_capacity: 20 # ephemeral tokens
buffer_window_secs: 600 # credit expiry
preempt_threshold_pct: 90 # start draining buffer at 90% base load
```

kevin (sales): Pricing ask: customers want predictable unit price for burst tokens. We should support both pay-as-you-go and prepaid bundles.

ella (customer success): For pilots we must include dashboard views and a single alert rule that surfaces "buffer depleted" and "buffer causing SLA pressure" to customer and our SREs.

maria (PM): Scope negotiation: minimal v1 = bookkeeping + allocator checks + billing events + simple console flag and alerts. v2 = UX for top-ups, expiry policies, and tenant billing UI.

sasha (SRE): Operational checklist item: simulate sustained bursts in staging to validate drain algorithm and ensure fallback to hosted API doesn't create feedback loops. Also define runbook for buffer-related incidents.

ajay (backend eng): Implementation risks: cross-tenant accounting bugs and race conditions during rapid bursts. We'll need feature-flag gating and a small unit test harness that replays concurrent allocations.

maria (PM): Decision points for next week sync: 1) accept per-pool+tenant accounting model? 2) confirm preempt rules (sasha proposed) 3) agree v1 launch criteria. Please react with :+1: if OK or comment objections.

kevin (sales): +1 from me — push for prepaid bundle option in v1 if possible.

ella (customer success): +1, but we need pilot dashboard view before external pilot.

ajay (backend eng): +1 but need a week to spike allocator changes.

sasha (SRE): +1, will author runbook draft and staging test plan.

ops-bot: Deployment note: feature-flag scaffold created on branch feat/elastic-buffer (CI passing).

maria (PM): Great — I'll write PRD with the v1/v2 split and action items. Action owners: ajay (allocator spike), sasha (runbook + SLO checks), ella (pilot dashboard requirements), kevin (pilot customer coordination). I'll share the PRD by EOD Friday.
